clue.text: Girl got married with no trepidation

parts.note: Una is a girl's name
to wed is to marry, so wed can mean married

explanation.surface: A girl went through her wedding without any nerves at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone undaunted is not filled with awe or fear, so acting without trepidation is the same idea.

clue.text: Pinned down with blows to the head

definitions.meaning: fixed or caught, as a fact or a culprit
driven home by hits on the head, as a nail is

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a nail being hammered on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail is to pin down exactly, and a nail is driven by blows to its head.

clue.text: What collier sports? Yes and no

definitions.text: What collier sports? Yes and no

indicators.note: a sport is a mutation, so to sport is to change form, and these letters change order

explanation.surface: Does a coal miner wear a certain kind of collar? Well, yes and no.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of WHAT COLLIER, rearranged, do give the answer; but a coal miner's collar would be grimy, and his work is the opposite of office work, hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: White-collar describes office workers, the very opposite of a manual worker such as a coal miner.

clue.text: Sensing disaster, demand loo is repaired

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone fears catastrophe and insists the toilet be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom-laden means heavy with foreboding, filled with a sense of coming disaster.

clue.text: Half an impasse

definitions.meaning: in rugby the fly-half position is also called by this hyphenated name
a deadlock in which neither side will give way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' looks like an instruction to take half of something, but it is a definition: in rugby union the stand-off half is the player who links the forwards and backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a rugby playing position known as a half, and a deadlocked confrontation.

clue.text: Central heating installed in chamber, one learned

indicators.note: installed in puts the heating letters inside the chamber word

parts.note: a solar is an upper private chamber in a medieval house
CH is the abbreviation for central heating, as in estate-agent listings

explanation.surface: Central heating has been fitted into a room belonging to an academic.
explanation.walkthrough: A solar (from Latin solarium) was the private upper room of a medieval manor.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person, someone with deep academic knowledge.

clue.text: Like girl's tribe

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
her is the possessive for a girl's

explanation.walkthrough: Asher was one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The tribe descended from Jacob's son Asher is one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

clue.text: A lot of noise in first half of meal

indicators.note: only the first half of the meal word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: There is a great racket during the early part of dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is a loud, prolonged noise.

clue.text: Fish left in sink

indicators.note: in places the left letter inside the sink word

parts.note: a ship founders when it sinks

explanation.surface: A fish has been left in the kitchen sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounder is a type of flatfish.

clue.text: Old European trip hard to inject with energy

indicators.note: the trip and hard letters are injected with the energy word, which goes inside them

parts.note: a visit is a short trip somewhere
go means energy or drive, as in get-up-and-go
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An old traveller from Europe needs some energy put into a gruelling journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Visigoths were a Germanic people of early medieval Europe, so one is an old European.

clue.text: Tribesman almost left, having waited

parts.note: a Hun was a member of a nomadic Asian tribe

indicators.note: almost signals that the word for left loses its last letter

parts.note: gone means having left

explanation.surface: A tribesman nearly departed after a long wait.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang on is an idiom for waiting a while, so the past form means waited.

clue.text: Make another series of changes in reversal of act

definitions.meaning: in bell-ringing a peal is a series of changes
revoking an Act of Parliament, cancelling a law

explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' are bell-ringing sequences: a peal is a long series of changes rung on church bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Revoking a law reverses an Act, and re-ringing a peal is a whimsical split of the same letters.

clue.text: Sitting at board, winning queen for knight? That's staggering

indicators.note: the word gains the queen letter in place of the knight letter, so it wins one at the other's expense

parts.note: board means a dining table, so sitting at it is lunching
N is the chess abbreviation for knight
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A chess player at the board wins a queen in exchange for a knight, and that is astonishing.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: 'board' is a dining table, and 'winning queen for knight' says swap the N for an R.
explanation.definitionFit: Lurching means staggering, swaying or reeling unsteadily from side to side.

clue.text: Darling, nurse this baby plant

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment like darling
to suckle is to nurse a baby at the breast

explanation.surface: A parent tells a loved one to feed this infant plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeysuckle is a climbing plant with sweet-scented flowers.

clue.text: Deplore trend bucked by unsuccessful claimant

indicators.note: a bucking horse throws itself about, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone laments a trend that was resisted by a failed pretender.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Pretender was James Francis Edward Stuart, who claimed the British throne in 1715 but never won it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Pretender claimed the British crown and failed, so he is a famous unsuccessful claimant.

clue.text: Have inconclusive discussion, but convince

definitions.meaning: to ... a subject is to discuss it without reaching the point
to talk someone round is to persuade them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both circling a topic without resolution and persuading someone to agree.

clue.text: Napoleon was this little of body

explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was nicknamed 'le petit caporal', the Little Corporal, by his troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's nickname used this military rank, and the same word as an adjective means bodily.

clue.text: Taking over marble for entertainment hall

parts.note: in cricket a bowler delivers an over, so taking an over is bowling
an alley is a kind of large playing marble

explanation.surface: A takeover of a marble-floored entertainment venue.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one bowler, so 'taking over' reads as bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowling alley is a building used for leisure where people bowl, so an entertainment hall.

clue.text: Fizzy cola given to dad for drink

indicators.note: a fizzy drink bubbles and churns, so the letters of cola are stirred up

parts.note: the word cola is taken as written and jumbled
pop is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: A bubbly soft drink is handed to father to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fizzy' looks like an adjective for cola, but it scrambles COLA into ALCO.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a sweet, fizzy, ready-mixed alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Sam's Sam, with an aunt in Oklahoma!

parts.note: Aunt Eller is a character in the musical Oklahoma!

explanation.surface: A man named Sam owns a servant also called Sam, who has an aunt in the musical Oklahoma!
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Weller is Samuel Pickwick's manservant in Dickens's The Pickwick Papers, hence 'Sam's Sam'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Pickwick's loyal servant in Dickens is named Sam, so he is Sam's Sam.

clue.text: Scattered police return to go over failed raid

indicators.note: the backward police word goes over, that is around, the jumbled raid
return means the police word is read backwards

parts.note: cops is slang for police

indicators.note: failed signals the letters of raid are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Police come back to look again at a raid that went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns COPS into SPOC; 'failed' makes RADI from RAID; 'to go over' wraps SPOC round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic means occurring at scattered, irregular intervals or places.

clue.text: Method of approach to secure new benefactor

indicators.note: to secure means the door word holds the new letter inside it

parts.note: a door is a way in, a means of approach

explanation.surface: A fresh way to win over a new patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor gives money or goods, so is a benefactor.

clue.text: Excited to find employment in bar

indicators.note: in places the employment word inside the bar word

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
use means employment, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to land a job working in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Roused means stirred up or excited, as feelings roused to anger.

clue.text: Whence Catherine, meanly dressed?

definitions.meaning: Catherine, Henry VIII's first wife, came from this Spanish kingdom
read as three words, a rag on, someone poorly clothed

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the name into A RAG ON, a whimsical picture of shabby dress; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine of Aragon came from that Spanish kingdom, and split up the name describes someone wearing a rag.

clue.text: Doctor stops unknown pain

indicators.note: stops means the doctor letters plug, that is enclose, the unknown letter

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
in algebra y is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A doctor puts an end to a mysterious ache.
explanation.walkthrough: GYP is British informal for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyp is a British colloquial word for pain or discomfort.

clue.text: How one plays lute with guts

definitions.meaning: a lute's strings are plucked, so it is played in a plucking way

explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' teases with lute strings made of gut, but here it means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucking is how a lute is played, and pluck is courage, so with guts means bravely.

clue.text: Rubbish from class getting suitable rebuke

parts.note: cl. is an abbreviation for class
apt means suitable
a rap is a sharp rebuke, as in a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: A class gets a well-deserved telling-off for talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is pretentious nonsense or empty talk, that is rubbish.

clue.text: Dull and tedious, but holding attention

indicators.note: holding means the tedious word contains the attention word

parts.note: dry means tedious or boring, as a dry lecture
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Something is boring and wearisome, yet it still grips the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull, gloomy and lacking interest.
